narrative.overview:
The household is an address: its one key number sits on a cobalt enamel plaque in tall signage numerals. Everything under the plaque is calm, native-feeling iOS: a porcelain ground, white inset grouped lists, and the system typeface.

Density is that of iOS Settings: rows of 56 to 60pt, one answer per screen at the top, recording actions second. The look it replaced (mint gradients, glass cards, a bouncy bubble tab bar, emoji in copy) is the confirmed anti-reference.
keyCharacteristics: One enamel field per tab screen, carrying exactly one key figure.
Signage numerals for money and counts; system type for every word.
Flat surfaces: depth comes from the enamel/porcelain/white tonal steps, not shadows.
Marigold appears only where something is yours.
Light and dark ("night enamel") share one structure; the header stays cobalt with white content in both.

rules.name: The One Plaque Rule
rules.body: Enamel owns one region per screen: the header field. It is not used for cards, banners or section backgrounds below it.

rules.name: The Yours Rule
rules.body: Marigold means "this is yours or your turn". It is never decoration, never text on white, and never a second brand colour.

rules.name: The Sign and Word Rule
rules.body: Owed and owe are never shown by colour alone: rows show "+" or "−" on the amount and a phrase ("Owes you", "You owe") beside it; the Home figure is captioned "You are owed" or "You owe".

rules.name: The Tertiary on White Rule
rules.body: In light, `text-tertiary` meets AA on `surface` (4.76:1) but not on `background` (4.36:1). Use `text-secondary` for small text set directly on the porcelain ground.

rules.name: The Numerals Only Rule
rules.body: The display face is used for money amounts, counts and tab-screen titles (plus the "Roomate" wordmark on the sign-in plaque). Never for body text, buttons, row titles or section headings. Never set `fontWeight` together with a `fonts.*` family.

rules.name: The Raised Cents Rule
rules.body: From 24pt up, `Amount` sets the currency sign at 42% (semibold, 80% opacity) and the cents at 45% of the figure size, both raised to the cap line. Below 24pt the whole amount sits on one baseline. Currency position and separators come from the device locale.

rules.name: The Scaling Rule
rules.body: All text goes through `AppText` and scales with Dynamic Type. Display numerals cap growth at 1.3x so they never clip; rows grow taller instead of truncating.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: A surface is separated by its fill, a hairline, or the sheet's curve. If it needs a shadow to read, it is on the wrong ground.

dos: Do give each tab screen one key figure on the enamel header and nothing else competing with it.
Do render every amount with `Amount`, and pass `direction` whenever the value is owed or owing.
Do pair every balance with its word ("Owes you", "You owe") next to the signed figure.
Do build content from `Group` and `GroupRow` on the porcelain sheet.
Do keep targets at 44pt and let rows grow with Dynamic Type.
Do read colours from `useThemeColors()` so both appearances stay in step.
donts: Don't use gradients, blur, glass cards or coloured glows.
Don't use emoji as icons or in copy.
Don't add uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow labels above headings. The plain sentence-case caption that names a key figure ("This month", "You are owed") is part of the figure, not an eyebrow.
Don't use marigold as decoration or as text on white.
Don't put more than one filled button in a view; the second action is the secondary (outlined) variant.
Don't set words in the display face or numerals for money in the system face.
Don't signal owe/owed, done/not done or an error by colour alone.
Don't add shadows or borders to light-mode groups.
